promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 8 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: This is a restart week, not a catch-up week. You are only just fever-free and still wiped out, so the plan has one gentle walk and two short walk-run sessions at most, with no missed runs added back.

flags.title: Missed runs after illness
flags.detail: Only the Mon Sep 7 run happened as planned. The Wed and Sat runs were lost to the fever, and I am not adding them back.

flags.title: Wednesday is a go or no-go
flags.detail: Run only if Tuesday's walk feels close to normal. If you are still wiped out or the cough sits in your chest, walk 20 min instead and try again Saturday.

flags.title: Effort on the run intervals
flags.detail: Monday's run felt 6/10 with heart rate mostly in zone 3. Keep the run minutes slow enough to talk in full sentences, even if that is slower than 7:40/km.

flags.title: Sleep
flags.detail: You averaged 6 hours last week, down from 7. Protect your sleep this week, because it helps you shake off the illness.

flags.title: Third weekly run
flags.detail: It stays off for now. It comes back next week only if both runs this week go smoothly.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No. Don't add the two missed runs, and don't go back to three runs yet.

A missed run can't be banked, and squeezing five runs into a week when you have just had a fever is the quickest way to a setback. This week is two short walk-run sessions at most, with a gentle walk first to see how you feel. If both go well, you return to your usual three mornings next week.

new.analysis:
Losing one week to a fever costs you very little fitness, and you have eight weeks to the race. You started in late August, so the gains so far are mostly your body getting used to running. A few days off will not undo that, but running while unwell or too soon can cost you several more weeks.

You are only about two days past your last fever, and you still have a cough and a blocked nose. You also say you feel wiped out. So the first job is to find out whether you can handle ordinary effort before asking for running effort. That is why the plan starts with a rest day and an easy walk, and why Wednesday's run is conditional. If anything is in your chest, or the fever comes back, that is a question for a doctor or pharmacist, not for me.

Your runs have been slower than they were hard. Your run intervals sit at 7:40/km, and your last three weeks of runs were effort 6 to 7 out of 10, with Monday's heart rate mostly in zone 3. For a first 5K where the goal is to run the whole way, that is a bit high for most sessions. On the return, keep the running minutes slow enough to talk, and slow down further or walk if your heart rate runs higher than usual. Finishing without walking comes from time on your feet at an easy effort, not from speed.

This week works as a lighter week, so the build has not stalled. If both runs go well, next week goes back to Mon, Wed and Sat with 2-minute run intervals. From there the run pieces stretch to 3, then 4 and 5 minutes, which keeps you on track for continuous running in the weeks before Nov 15. If a few more days are needed, I would rather repeat a week than rush it.

safetyCallouts.title: Get the fever and cough checked if they do not settle.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a fever of 38.4 and are still coughing and blocked up. If the fever returns, or you get chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness, stop running and see a doctor or pharmacist. Do the same if the cough is not clearly improving by the end of this week. I can't say what is behind it, so that call is not mine.
